subtitulo: Shorter sentences in a news report
descripcion: At B2 the basic reduction of a relative clause is learned: dropping the pronoun and auxiliary when the clause is passive or continuous, as long as the missing pronoun would be the subject. The C1 refinement of combining this with nominalisation in dense reports isn't the focus here.

ejemplos.texto: The email sent this morning hasn't been answered yet.
Anyone waiting outside should come in now.
The people invited to the meeting already know the agenda.

notas: The reduction only works when the missing pronoun would be the subject of its own clause, not the object.
Passive clauses reduce with the past participle; active continuous clauses reduce with the -ing form.
This is mostly a written structure; in speech, the full relative clause is usually more natural.

es.en: Spanish does not reduce relative clauses this way in speech; que usually stays. Spanish speakers therefore tend to keep the full relative clause in English even where the reduced form would be more natural and compact.
es.es: En el habla, el español no reduce las oraciones de relativo de esta manera; normalmente mantiene «que». Por eso, los hispanohablantes tienden a conservar la relativa completa en inglés incluso cuando una forma reducida sería más natural y compacta.

de.en: German compresses with a participle placed before the noun (der dort sitzende Mann), so the English postnominal reduction (the man sitting over there) has no German model. German speakers either keep the full relative clause or produce a calque such as the there sitting man.
de.de: Deutsch verdichtet mit einem Partizip vor dem Substantiv («der dort sitzende Mann»), daher hat die englische Nachstellung («the man sitting over there») kein direktes deutsches Modell. Deutschsprachige behalten oft den vollständigen Relativsatz oder bilden eine wörtliche Form wie «the there sitting man».

it.en: Reduced passive relatives are easy, since Italian uses the same postnominal participle (i documenti inviati ieri – the documents sent yesterday). Reductions with -ing are harder, because Italian rarely uses the present participle this way and keeps a relative clause instead (l'uomo che parla).
it.it: Le relative passive ridotte sono facili, perché l'italiano usa lo stesso participio dopo il nome («i documenti inviati ieri» – «the documents sent yesterday»). Le riduzioni in «-ing» sono più difficili, perché l'italiano usa raramente il participio presente in questo modo e mantiene una relativa («l'uomo che parla»).

fr.en: French has both reduction types: the postnominal past participle (les documents envoyés hier) and, in formal style, the participe présent (les étudiants travaillant ici). French speakers therefore reduce relative clauses easily; the risk is using the -ing form where English needs a full clause.
fr.fr: Le français possède les deux types de réduction : le participe passé postposé («les documents envoyés hier») et, dans un style formel, le participe présent («les étudiants travaillant ici»). Les francophones réduisent donc facilement les relatives ; le risque est d'utiliser la forme en «-ing» là où l'anglais exige une proposition complète.

pt.en: Reduced passive relatives are easy, since Portuguese uses the same postnominal participle (os documentos enviados ontem). Brazilian Portuguese also uses the gerúndio adjectivally (uma caixa contendo livros), which is a good bridge to -ing reductions (a box containing books).
pt.pt: As relativas passivas reduzidas são fáceis, pois o português usa o mesmo particípio depois do substantivo («os documentos enviados ontem»). O português brasileiro também usa o gerúndio com valor adjetival («uma caixa contendo livros»), uma boa ponte para reduções em «-ing» («a box containing books»).

errores: Trying to reduce a clause where the missing pronoun is the object, which isn't grammatically allowed.
Using the wrong participle: active -ing where a passive past participle is needed, or vice versa.
Using this reduced form in casual speech, where it can sound unnecessarily formal.

es: Using *-ing* after the noun for a single finished action: *the letter arriving yesterday* instead of *the letter that arrived yesterday*.
de: Placing the participle phrase before the noun: *the in Zurich living people* instead of *the people living in Zurich*.
it: *proveniente da* rendered as *provenient from*: *the train provenient from Milan* instead of *coming from Milan*.
fr: *en provenance de* rendered as *in provenance of*: *the train in provenance of Lyon* instead of *coming from Lyon*.
pt: *proveniente de* rendered as *provenient from*: *the train provenient from Porto* instead of *coming from Porto*.

traducciones.pt: qualquer pessoa que esteja à espera…

redemittel.expresion: Can I drop the pronoun here?
redemittel.funcion: tests whether the clause can be reduced

traducciones.de: Kann ich das Pronomen hier weglassen?

mision.consigna: Write a short news report about a false story that spread online.
requisitos: one sentence where you keep *who* or *which* because it's needed

microtareas.texto: Write five sentences with *which was* or *who is*, then cut them.
Three sentences about a *headline* with a participle.
Record 90 seconds: why does *fake news* spread?

autochequeo: Is the reduction only used where the missing pronoun would be the subject?
Is the active/passive participle chosen correctly?
Does the reduction suit the register of the text (writing, not casual speech)?
Are at least three reduced clauses used?
Would a full relative clause sound more natural anywhere I used a reduced one?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on reduced relative clauses. Check whether each reduction is grammatically allowed and whether the participle form is correct. Do not rewrite the text.
